rationale: The workflow runs on push and pull_request to main with a single build-and-smoke job, so P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE applies: runs on the same branch/PR represent the same workflow and a newer revision supersedes older checks. Adding a concurrency group keyed by github.workflow and github.ref with cancel-in-progress cancels in-progress superseded runs when a new revision arrives, avoiding duplicate work while the latest run still executes the full build and test suite, so intended coverage is preserved. Preconditions are met (same workflow/branch/PR; newer revision supersedes). Contraindications are avoided: this is build/test, not release or deployment, and keying by github.ref means distinct branches do not share a cancellation group. Permissions stay contents: read; no new actions, secrets, publishing/deployment, or network access are added. Other patterns were checked and rejected: P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not added because an equivalent npm dependency cache already exists via setup-node cache; P-LIT-FAIL-FAST needs a matrix, which is absent; P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is not safely applied because no representative successful-duration history is available and the Docker test steps make an arbitrary fixed timeout (e.g. the 5 minutes in the measured experiment) likely to exceed valid slow runs.
